title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN K-12 EDUCATION: ALIGNMENT WITH STATE CURRICULUM STANDARDS AND STUDENT PERSONAS

bias_targets.methodology: Varying the user's home state in the prompt and analyzing the generated response's ideological framing and content alignment with that specific state's curriculum standards for U.S. history.

Correlating the LLMs' alignment with state historical curricula against the political affiliations and voting patterns (red, blue, swing states) of those states to see if models infer and adapt to perceived political leanings.

Varying the student's grade level (elementary, middle, high school) in the prompt and evaluating response divergence by measuring average token length, sentiment (via a RoBERTa-based classifier), and text complexity (Flesch-Kincaid grade level score).
Varying the student's gender (male, female) in the prompt and evaluating response divergence by measuring average token length, sentiment score, and Flesch-Kincaid text complexity.
Varying the student's race (White, Black, Hispanic, Asian) in the prompt and evaluating response divergence by measuring average token length, sentiment score, and Flesch-Kincaid text complexity.
